markdown.markdown:
In this section, I want to preserve the footprints—and the people—that led me to build this website. I started making websites when I was around ten, not in a formal or particularly skillful way, but I wrote plenty of blog-style posts. Recently, I realized it was time to start over. This reboot feels like a small reconnaissance mission—driven by nostalgia for how blogs worked and how authors connected from roughly 2000 to 2010. It was a golden era, before social media and today’s wave of AI-generated noise.  

## CMS
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org) is recommended by [Dr. Marcelo Leal](https://www.marcelomleal.com/) at my university. 
- [Blowfish](https://blowfish.page/) was the theme I used for my previous [Hugo](https://gohugo.io/) website. It's brilliant and easy to customize.
- I have used [WordPress](https://wordpress.org) for nearly two decades, including theme customization and plugin modifications.

## Inspirations
- [Dr. Andrew Heiss](https://www.andrewheiss.com/) is incredibly productive and shares many practical tips for organizing an academic website. His posts go back to 2007—it’s impressive that he has preserved so many digital footprints.
- [Dr. David Folio](https://dfolio.fr/) taught me [how to create a custom publication listing](https://dfolio.fr/posts/2023/2023-08-17_publications.html) with Quarto. Merci beaucoup.
- [justfont](https://justfont.com/huninn/) designed [Hunnin](https://justfont.com/huninn/), an open font based on [Kosugi Maru](https://github.com/googlefonts/kosugi-maru) and [Varela Round](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Varela+Round). Hunnin is super friendly for [Tâi-uân Lô-má-jī Phing-im Hong-àn](https://encyclopedia.pub/entry/33540) (Taiwanese Romanization System) and is on both [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Huninn?preview.text=L%C3%AD-h%C3%B3,%20tsia%CC%8Dh-p%C3%A1%E2%80%93bu%C4%93%3F%20&query=Justfont) and [GitHub](https://github.com/justfont/open-huninn-font).

# Career

I served in the military for 12 years before pursuing my Ph.D. Below are selected positions I’ve held and training and certifications I’ve completed. Feel free to reach out if you’d like to talk further. 

## Position
- Foreign Affairs Liaison Officer (Apr. 2025 – Aug. 2025).
- General Staff (Mar. 2025 – Apr. 2025).
- Battalion Counselor (Jul. 2022 – Sep. 2024).
- Public Affairs Officer (Sep. 2019 – Jun. 2022).
- Company Counselor and Platoon Leader (Jul. 2012 – Aug. 2014).

## Certifications
- Program on Terrorism and Security Studies, George C. Marshall European Center for Security Studies.
- Psychological Operations Qualification Course Certification, USAJFKSWCS (Jun. 2018). [Summary Report](https://report.nat.gov.tw/ReportFront/ReportDetail/detail?sysId=C10700199).
- American Language Course, Defense Language Institute (Apr. 2018).
- Captain Career Course, Political Warfare Education and Training Center (Dec. 2017).
- Fire Manager Training, Army Engineering School (Nov. 2012).
- Advanced Summertime Training, Army Infantry School (Aug. 2010).
- Basic Summertime Training, Army Infantry School (Aug. 2009).
- Basic Military Training, Army Infantry School (Aug. 2008).

# Extracurricular Activities
Beyond my professional roles, I enjoy exploring creativity as an amateur web and graphic designer, and I occasionally dabble in music. I also try not to play too many video games 🎮.

## Volunteer Activities

- Volunteer, Yunshui Community Development Association, Chiayi County (Aug. 2018 – Present).
- Music performer, Da-Wo Veterans Home (Jan. 2012).
- Music performer, Banqiao Veterans Home (Jan. 2011).
- Music performer, Taoyuan Veterans Home (Sep. 2010).
- Documentary production and community service, Da-Ai Indigenous Tribe (Aug. 2009).

## Graduate School
- Served as the Chief of Multimedia Products at the [2015 MND News Summer Camp for High Schoolers](https://n.yam.com/Article/20150703132977), overseeing the production of multimedia content.
- Translated Chapter 4, *“On the Move,”* of the book [*Computing without Computers*](https://teachinglondoncomputing.org/resources/inspiring-computing-stories/computingwithoutcomputers/) (Taiwanese Mandarin title: [不用電腦學程式](http://paperplane-tw.weebly.com/cdc.html)), adapting complex concepts for local readers.
- Localized the video game [**Gone Home**](https://fullbright.company/localization/) by The Fullbright Game Company into Taiwanese Mandarin, making it accessible to a broader audience.
- Adapted [**Firefly**](https://crowdin.com/project/firefly-iii), a personal finance management application built on Laravel, for Taiwanese Mandarin speakers, enhancing user experience and accessibility.

## Undergraduate
- Served as an Intern Political Warfare Officer in the Cadet Corps, leading various strategic initiatives (Feb. 2011 – Feb. 2012).
- Acted as the College Flag Bearer in the Color Guard, representing the college in numerous ceremonial duties (Jul. 2011 – Jan. 2012).
- Participated in the 2012 University Communication Basketball Cup as a member of the departmental basketball team (May 2012).
- Represented the Cadet Corps in visits to three U.S. military institutes—[Virginia Military Institute (VMI)](https://www.vmi.edu/), [United States Military Academy (USMA)](https://www.westpoint.edu/), and [The Citadel](https://www.citadel.edu/)—enhancing international military exchanges (Aug. 2010).
- Served as Director of the Rock 'n’ Roll Club, organizing events and managing club operations (Jul. 2010 – Jul. 2011).
- Participated as an assistant performer in [the opening ceremony](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2cFJBkq0c_I) of the 2009 Summer Deaflympics at Taipei Stadium, Taiwan (Sep. 2009).
- Performed as a member of the Fu Hsing Kang Choir in diverse venues (Oct. 2008 – Jun. 2009).
